title: Priv EKS Terraform module: upgrade guardian and live health hooks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a hardened Terraform module for Redwood Private control plane provisioning that ensures non-disruptive cluster upgrades, automated preflight health checks, and safe rollback paths. Goals: 1) idempotent provisioning across accounts and regions, 2) pre-upgrade validation hooks (network, KMS, IAM, control-plane node readiness), 3) automated canary/partial upgrade flow for control plane and critical nodegroups, 4) integration with observability/alerting for upgrade regressions, and 5) documented runbook and migration steps for existing customers. Acceptance criteria: module published in private registry, example stacks in infra-examples repo, e2e upgrade test passing in staging, at least two Datadog monitors and one dashboard for upgrade health, and a documented terraform state migration plan.
updates: 2026-01-27: Kickoff meeting with infra, platform, and security. Agreed on scope: control-plane immutability during upgrade window, separate IAM role for module execution, S3 backend with state locking via DynamoDB.

2026-02-02: Design decision: use resource-level 'create_before_destroy' for nodegroups where possible; control-plane upgrades use EKS recommended sequence with cordon/drain of workload nodegroups handled outside module. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Priv+EKS+Upgrade+Guardian (internal).

2026-02-10: Prototype module created at git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-terraform-modules.git::modules/priv-eks-guardian. Initial tests show idempotent apply across repeated runs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform-modules/pull/412

2026-02-18: Implemented preflight probe hooks: network reachability (VPC endpoints), KMS key access check, IAM policy boundaries, and required ENI quotas. Probe results surfaced as Terraform plan warnings. Added unit tests for probe scripts.

2026-02-24: Healthhook lambda added to run post-apply smoke checks against kube-apiserver /healthz and control-plane metrics. Lambda runs as part of the module via null_resource local-exec with retry/backoff. Iterating on timeout values (currently 10m).

2026-03-01: Integration with observability: created Datadog monitors for apiserver latency, etcd leader changes, and control-plane API error spikes. Dashboard draft: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/priv-eks-upgrade-health (internal).

2026-03-05: Internal review with Security: KMS key access must be optional flag (enable_kms_check = true/false) for air-gapped installs; added encryption_at_rest_validation step. Security requested an IAM permissions table in the README. Action: @Ryan to add by 2026-03-10.

2026-03-09: Canary strategy defined: 10% of control-plane endpoints (subset of clusters) upgraded first with traffic routed via smart-router and fallback policy. Canary rollout is orchestrated by the console rollout API (integration ticket planned).

2026-03-11: E2E staging run (cluster-staging-3): upgrade applied using module v0.1.0-canary. Observed brief increase in apiserver 5xx errors for 30s, Datadog alert threshold triggered — conditions captured and playbook updated. Rollback tested by restoring previous terraform state and reapplying module; procedure took ~12 minutes. Post-incident: add pre-warm of api-server endpoint and extended drain window in runbook.

2026-03-12: PR 412 updated with fixes from staging. Requesting final review from @Leah Park (platform) and @Marco Diaz (SRE). Next steps: publish module to private registry, add example overlays in infra-examples, and schedule rollout rehearsal with solutions engineering.
